specialties.why: Epithelioid sarcoma is a rare soft tissue sarcoma with proximal and distal types, so a sarcoma-focused oncology team is a relevant kind of service.
specialties.plain: Look for cancer doctors who focus on sarcoma, since this is a rare soft tissue cancer.

specialties.why: Reports describe epithelioid sarcoma patients being referred to and managed at tertiary orthopaedic sarcoma units.
specialties.plain: Look for surgeons at sarcoma units that see this tumor.

specialties.why: Diagnosis relies on immunostains such as loss of INI1/SMARCB1, and the tumor can be confused with other epithelioid tumors.
specialties.plain: A pathologist who knows sarcoma can check the tissue tests, because this tumor can look like other conditions.

centerCapabilities.text: Pathology review that includes INI1/SMARCB1 immunostaining, since loss of this protein is a defining feature of epithelioid sarcoma.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center can test tissue for loss of INI1/SMARCB1.

centerCapabilities.text: A dedicated tertiary sarcoma unit that treats epithelioid sarcoma and tracks outcomes in a maintained database.
centerCapabilities.plain: A sarcoma unit that sees many cases and keeps careful records.

centerCapabilities.text: Familiarity with this tumor's recognised potential for lymph node involvement and repeated local recurrence.
centerCapabilities.plain: The team knows this tumor can spread to lymph nodes and come back locally.

redFlags.text: A service that has no sarcoma pathology input, since this tumor can look like other lesions, including cysts, abscesses and other SMARCB1-deficient or vascular tumors.
redFlags.plain: Be careful if no sarcoma pathologist checks the tissue. This tumor can look like other things.

redFlags.text: A service with little or no experience with epithelioid sarcoma, which sources describe as rare and lacking a defined optimal long-term management strategy.
redFlags.plain: Be careful with places that rarely see this tumor.

trialEligibility.text: Listings typically ask for confirmed epithelioid sarcoma diagnosis, which depends on pathology findings such as complete loss of INI1/SMARCB1.
trialEligibility.plain: Trials often need a confirmed diagnosis from tissue tests.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may ask about loss of SMARCB1/INI1 or other SWI/SNF complex proteins, which characterizes epithelioid sarcoma.
trialEligibility.plain: Some trials may ask about SMARCB1/INI1 results.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may specify proximal or distal type, which sources describe as having different biology.
trialEligibility.plain: Trials may say whether they accept proximal or distal type.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may distinguish localized disease from advanced or metastatic disease, and may ask about lymph node involvement.
trialEligibility.plain: Trials often ask whether the cancer is local or has spread.

supportNeeds.text: GARD, the NIH rare disease information service, lists epithelioid sarcoma and offers a rare disease information line at 1-888-205-2311.
supportNeeds.plain: GARD has a phone line for rare disease questions: 1-888-205-2311.

questions.text: How many patients with epithelioid sarcoma have you or your team treated?
Can you review my pathology, including INI1/SMARCB1 results, and tell me if outside slides need a second review?
Do you have a dedicated sarcoma unit and a pathologist who reviews epithelioid sarcoma cases?
Can your center confirm whether my tumor is proximal-type or distal-type?
Does this trial require documented loss of SMARCB1/INI1 and a specific epithelioid sarcoma type?
Which disease stage or lymph node findings does this trial accept?
What information or community resources do you have for people with epithelioid sarcoma?
